name: Apply AHE to TanStack chat harness while keeping bundle lean

description: Baseline AHE session setup and current chat harness bundle measurement

asi.hypothesis: Establish an observability-driven loop inspired by AHE: explicit files in scope, reproducible bundle metric, and typecheck backpressure before changing harness structure.
asi.paper_applied: Mapped AHE component/experience/decision observability to autoresearch.md scope, METRIC output, checks, and ASI hypotheses.
asi.user_changes_note: Repository had pre-existing uncommitted chat changes; baseline keep records the current app state plus autoresearch harness on the autoresearch branch.

description: Replace heavy markdown dependency path with lightweight safe inline renderer

asi.hypothesis: AHE structural simplification: markdown rendering is a component-level harness service; replacing general GFM dependencies with a focused renderer for chat needs should preserve common formatting while reducing client payload.
asi.outcome: Large primary improvement by removing react-markdown/remark-gfm from the client import graph; typecheck and build still pass.
asi.tradeoff: Renderer supports paragraphs, ordered/unordered lists, fenced code, inline code, and http/mailto links, but not full GFM tables/task lists. This is acceptable for tutorial chat unless full GFM is a hard requirement.

description: Replace Radix controls with native form controls for lean harness UI

asi.hypothesis: Component observability exposed Radix Select/Toggle/Tooltip/ScrollArea as heavyweight UI harness components. Native select/button/title/scroll containers should preserve tutorial functionality and accessibility while reducing dependencies in the client graph.
asi.outcome: Primary bundle metric improved substantially; build and typecheck pass. Native controls keep model selection, toggles, scrolling, and send/stop affordances.
asi.tradeoff: Custom popper styling/check icons/tooltips were simplified to browser-native controls; acceptable because behavior remains clear and the app becomes more transferable/less framework-specific.

description: Split client request-search tool definition from server-only tool implementations

asi.hypothesis: AHE component observability suggests client and server tool components need explicit file boundaries. Moving request_search_query to a small shared module should keep the client from pulling demo weather/stock/Brave server tool definitions into the route chunk.
asi.outcome: Bundle improved modestly; build and typecheck pass. Client Chat now imports only the interactive tool definition it actually needs.
asi.transferable_lesson: File-level component boundaries matter for bundlers: mixed client/server tool modules can leak unnecessary harness structure into browser code.

description: Use plain JSON Schema for browser-side interactive tool definition

asi.hypothesis: Decision observability from the prior split showed the remaining shared client tool still carried Zod. TanStack AI accepts plain JSON Schema, so using JSON Schema for the client-visible request_search_query contract should preserve provider/tool metadata while dropping Zod from browser bundles.
asi.outcome: Large improvement; build and typecheck pass. The schema remains explicit and serializable, matching AHE's preference for file-level, inspectable component contracts.
asi.tradeoff: Lost Zod-inferred static arg typing for this one client tool definition, but Chat already narrows tool input at runtime and the schema contract remains precise.

description: Try plain client tool object instead of toolDefinition.client wrapper

asi.hypothesis: A plain AnyClientTool-shaped object might avoid importing toolDefinition code into the browser while preserving the client tool contract.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed slightly; likely because the shared request-search-tool module still imports toolDefinition for the server definition, so the client chunk did not avoid the import and added wrapper code.
asi.next_action_hint: If revisiting, split schema constants into a third module that has no @tanstack/ai import, with separate server definition and client plain-object factory files.

description: Split request-search schema constants and use plain client tool object

asi.hypothesis: Separating schema constants from the server toolDefinition import should let the browser use a plain client tool object without pulling server definition code.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric still regressed slightly versus the prior best; @tanstack/ai-react/@tanstack/ai-client likely already bring the relevant runtime, and the extra factory/module boundary adds overhead.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the simpler toolDefinition.client setup. Focus next on actual route/UI code or server bundle rather than this micro-split.

description: Remove identity clientTools wrapper and unused AG-UI status local

asi.hypothesis: Experience from the previous failed micro-splits suggests avoiding extra identity helpers may yield small wins without changing harness behavior. useChat accepts the tool array directly, and latestAgUiStatus was unused.
asi.outcome: Small primary improvement; typecheck confirms the direct tools array is accepted.
asi.transferable_lesson: Prefer direct data contracts over convenience wrappers when the wrapper is only an identity function in hot client harness code.

description: Export TanStack Start handler directly from server entry

asi.hypothesis: Component observability shows the server entry wrapped the TanStack Start fetch handler without adding behavior. Removing this adapter should slightly reduce harness surface area and bundle output while preserving semantics.
asi.outcome: Tiny primary improvement; build and typecheck pass.
asi.transferable_lesson: AHE-style component audits can safely delete pass-through middleware when it has no observability or policy function.

description: Trim redundant false debug flags from chat server route

asi.hypothesis: Decision observability in the chat middleware should keep only active diagnostics. Explicit false debug fields add serialized code surface without changing behavior if defaults are false.
asi.outcome: Tiny primary improvement; error logging remains enabled through the custom logger.
asi.risk_note: Assumes TanStack AI debug defaults are false for omitted fields, consistent with the previous explicit configuration.

description: Factor tool label ternary into helper

asi.hypothesis: Replacing a long inline ternary with a helper might reduce repeated render code and improve component readability without changing behavior.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed; helper function overhead outweighed any minification benefit for a single call site.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not factor single-use render expressions purely for bundle size. Only extract when there are multiple call sites or readability is worth neutral/slight cost.

description: Replace server tool Zod schemas with plain JSON Schema

asi.hypothesis: Using plain JSON Schema for all server tool definitions might remove Zod from the server bundle, mirroring the successful browser-side request_search_query change.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed; Zod was apparently not materially bundled in the measured server output or the verbose JSON Schema literals outweighed any removal.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep Zod for server-only tools where it improves maintainability and inferred contracts. Plain JSON Schema is only beneficial for client-visible schemas.

description: Remove StrictMode wrapper from production hydration entry

asi.hypothesis: The client entry's StrictMode wrapper is a development diagnostic component, not core harness behavior. Removing it from this tutorial production entry should slightly reduce client code without affecting production semantics.
asi.outcome: Tiny primary improvement; build and typecheck pass.
asi.risk_note: React StrictMode's extra development checks are no longer applied at runtime. If this project relies on StrictMode during local dev, consider a dev-only wrapper instead.

description: Hydrate StartClient directly without startTransition wrapper

asi.hypothesis: The hydration entry can be a direct component handoff; startTransition is another pass-through wrapper that adds code but does not change steady-state chat harness behavior.
asi.outcome: Tiny primary improvement; build and typecheck pass.
asi.risk_note: If future startup work becomes expensive, a transition wrapper could be reintroduced for scheduling. Current entry has no visible pending UI to benefit from it.

description: Remove scrollRestoration option from single-page chat router

asi.hypothesis: For this single-page chat tutorial, router scroll restoration is not a meaningful harness capability. Removing the option should slightly reduce route/router configuration surface without affecting current navigation behavior.
asi.outcome: Tiny primary improvement; build and typecheck pass.
asi.risk_note: If the app grows multiple scrollable routes, revisit scroll restoration as a UX feature rather than a default.

asi.hypothesis: A trust-but-filter helper for server-generated follow-up events might be smaller than a Boolean type guard with Array.every validation while preserving runtime safety.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed slightly; the filter helper added more code than the compact Boolean guard after minification/gzip.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing custom event guard. Avoid micro-optimizing validation code unless it removes a dependency or repeated branch.
